Async ingestion

An event feed, a finite file, a batch job and a gRPC client can all supply the same ordered asynchronous sequence.

Contract illustration
Input
◉ Active+ Added− RemovedΔ Changed× Rejected
The rule
What the contract requires
Preserve the input order, event boundaries and logical-time controls when changing batch sizes.
The boundary
Scope and constraints
Each record in a transport batch can be accepted or rejected. Each projection commits its changes independently.
Example · C#
Consume an input stream
Full source ↗
Supply events or batches through the same async port. Handle each receipt.
UsageExamples.cs
public static async Task ConsumeInputsAsync(
    IProjectionEngine engine, IAsyncEnumerable<EngineInput> input,
    Func<IngestResult, CancellationToken, ValueTask> handleReceipt,
    CancellationToken ct)
{
    // input may yield NativeBatchInput with one record or many records.
    // A file reader or event transport supplies the same async contract.
    await foreach (var receipt in engine.IngestAsync(input, ct).WithCancellation(ct))
        await handleReceipt(receipt, ct); // Handle acceptance AND rejection.
    // Acceptance does not mean that every downstream projection committed.
    // Observe committed graph changes through IGraphSpace.SubscribeAsync.
}
Compile-checked caller example. Execution requires implementations of the injected interfaces.

public interface IProjectionEngine
{
    IAsyncEnumerable<IngestResult> IngestAsync(IAsyncEnumerable<EngineInput> input,
        CancellationToken cancellationToken = default);
    IAsyncEnumerable<ConfigurationReceipt> ConfigureAsync(IAsyncEnumerable<ConfigurationCommand> commands,
        CancellationToken cancellationToken = default);
    IAsyncEnumerable<TelemetryObservation> ObserveTelemetryAsync(IAsyncEnumerable<TelemetrySubscription> projections,
        CancellationToken cancellationToken = default);
}
